title: Truganini
summary: Truganini, a Palawa woman of Tasmania, was born on Bruny Island about 1812 and died in Hobart in 1876. After her death her bones were put on display at the Tasmanian Museum until 1947. In 1976 her ashes were scattered on the waters of the D'Entrecasteaux Channel.

uncertainty.note: Both opened pages say she was born "about" or "around" 1812.

where.modern_name: Bruny Island, Tasmania, Australia; pinned to her birthplace and homeland (she died in Hobart)
where.historical_name: Bruny Island, Van Diemen's Land (British colony)

importance.justification: Her life and the museum display of her bones after death are widely told in Australian museum histories of Tasmanian Aboriginal people.

audience_note: Includes the display of a Tasmanian Aboriginal woman's remains as a museum specimen, a subject that may distress Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander viewers.

sources.title: OpenStreetMap Nominatim result for Bruny Island

reviewer_note: Spelling varies; the National Portrait Gallery notes Trukanini is the spelling used by the Palawa people. Sources differ on the end of the display (1947 per the Australian Museum), so only that date is used. Review wording with Aboriginal community guidance.
